title: Student unaware of data sharing implications
description: Student may not be fully aware of what data is being shared (work file, student id, course, timestamp) and how it will be used by the Grades Portal Web App.
assumptions: Student may not have read privacy policies or understand data usage

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Data in transit between Student and Grades Portal Web App could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, compromising confidentiality of work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp.
assumptions: Data may be transmitted over potentially insecure network

title: Metadata leakage for party linking
description: Meta-data about the parties (student id, course) in the data flow could be used to link or identify students across different systems or sessions.
assumptions: Metadata may be exposed during transmission

title: Unauthorized access to submitted data
description: Grades Portal Web App may not adequately protect submitted data from unauthorized access, potentially exposing student work, identifiers, and submission information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: System may lack proper access controls

title: Data tampering or falsification
description: Grades Portal Web App may not properly validate or detect falsified data submitted by students, potentially allowing incorrect or deceptive submissions.
assumptions: System may lack robust data validation mechanisms

title: Sharing of student identifiers
description: Portal shares student id, course, file reference, and requesting role - unique references to student identity that enable identification of data subjects
assumptions: Student identifiers are transmitted as part of the submission/grading request

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Student identifiers and file references transmitted between P1 and P2 could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, compromising confidentiality of identifiable data
assumptions: Data flows over network without guaranteed encryption

title: Processing of identified data
description: Assignment & Grading Service processes student identifiers, course information, and file references, which could enable tracking or profiling of students
assumptions: P2 uses the received identifiers for grading and record-keeping purposes

title: Attribution of grading actions
description: Requesting role and file reference data enable attribution of grading actions to specific individuals, creating non-repudiation concerns if actions are disputed
assumptions: Grading actions are linked to student identifiers and requesting roles

title: Excessive Data Collection at Source
description: The grading service may collect and store more personal data than strictly necessary for the assignment submission process, violating the minimality principle. Student ID, course, and submission time are collected, but additional metadata or derived information may be included without clear necessity.

title: Data Leakage During Transfer
description: Personal data (student ID, course, submission time) transmitted from the grading service to the data store may be intercepted or exposed during transit, potentially through network vulnerabilities or insecure transmission protocols.

title: Data Disclosure at Destination
description: The assignment store may disclose student data to third parties (e.g., course administrators, external evaluators) without explicit consent or necessity, or may retain data beyond the required retention period.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Data
description: The data store may be vulnerable to unauthorized access by malicious actors or compromised accounts, leading to potential exposure of student personal information.

title: Data Integrity Compromise at Destination
description: Stored assignment data may be corrupted, altered, or tampered with by unauthorized parties, affecting the authenticity and reliability of the submitted work.

title: Teacher identification through login
description: Teacher's identity is identified and recorded when logging into the system, creating a persistent identifier that can be used to track and profile the teacher's activities across the platform.
assumptions: Teacher provides credentials that uniquely identify them in the system

title: Unintended data sharing by teacher
description: Teacher may inadvertently share more data than intended when requesting submission queue, potentially exposing course information or student data through the login process.
assumptions: Teacher may not fully understand the scope of data being shared through their login and request

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Teacher-submission data in transit between teacher and grades portal could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive course and student information.
assumptions: Data flows over potentially insecure network connections

title: Meta-data identification in transit
description: Meta-data about the parties (teacher and system) in the data flow could be used to link and identify the teacher's activities and preferences.
assumptions: Network meta-data (timestamps, packet sizes, etc.) is captured and analyzed

title: System identification of teacher
description: Grades portal system identifies and records the teacher's identity upon login, creating a persistent identifier that enables tracking of all teacher activities and submissions reviewed.
assumptions: System maintains teacher identity records and links them to all activities

title: Potential disclosure of submission data
description: Grades portal may disclose teacher-submission data to unauthorized parties or in ways not intended by the teacher, potentially exposing sensitive course and student information.
assumptions: System may have inadequate access controls or data sharing policies

title: Lawful basis for student data sharing
description: Portal may share student data with teachers without proper legal basis, consent, or authorization as required by educational privacy regulations (e.g., FERPA, GDPR).

title: Information sharing beyond necessity
description: Portal may share more student information than necessary for the intended purpose (e.g., submission times, metadata) which could enable tracking or profiling.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Portal may not comply with applicable data protection regulations regarding student data sharing with teachers, including data minimization and purpose limitation principles.

title: Teacher may use data beyond intended purpose
description: Teacher may use student data for purposes beyond the intended educational assessment (e.g., administrative tracking, external sharing) without proper authorization.

title: Unintended consequences of data access
description: Teacher access to student data may lead to unintended consequences such as bias in grading, discrimination, or inappropriate use of student information.

title: Unauthorized data disclosure at source
description: The grading service may share grade records with unauthorized recipients or without proper authorization controls, potentially exposing sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has appropriate access controls and authorization mechanisms in place.

title: Intrusion into source data handling
description: Malicious actors may attempt to intercept or manipulate the grade records before they are transmitted to the database, potentially altering or corrupting sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service processes data in a manner that could be vulnerable to interception or manipulation.

title: Data interception during transit
description: Grade records in transit between the grading service and database may be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive student information including grades and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may not be adequately protected by encryption or other security measures.

title: Unauthorized data access at destination
description: The grade records database may be accessed by unauthorized users or systems, potentially leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive student information.
assumptions: Assumes the database has appropriate access controls and security measures in place.

title: Unintended data retention or processing
description: The database may retain or process grade records in ways that were not intended, potentially leading to unintended consequences for student privacy.
assumptions: Assumes the database may have unintended data retention or processing behaviors.

title: Student request identifies student
description: The student's request for grades inherently identifies the student as the data subject, which may be a privacy concern if the request is made without proper authentication or if the request itself reveals sensitive information about the student's academic status.
assumptions: Student is authenticated to make the request

title: Data flow reveals identifying information
description: The data flow itself may contain metadata that identifies the student (e.g., request patterns, timing, IP address) which could be used to link or identify the student even if the actual grades are not exposed.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over a network that may be monitored

title: System processes identifying information
description: The Grades Portal Web App processes the student's identifying information when retrieving and displaying grades, which requires appropriate access controls and data protection measures.
assumptions: System has proper authentication and authorization mechanisms

title: Lawfulness of data sharing
description: The Grades Portal Web App may not have proper legal basis or consent for sharing student grades and feedback data with the student.

title: Information quality concerns
description: The grades and teacher feedback displayed may be inaccurate, outdated, or contain errors, potentially misleading the student.

title: Insufficient notice
description: The student may not be properly informed about what data is being shared, how it will be used, or the purposes of the data processing.

title: Data in transit metadata exposure
description: Metadata about the parties (student and portal) in the data flow could potentially be used to link or identify the student.

title: Unintended data processing at destination
description: The student may process or use the received grades and feedback in ways that are not intended or authorized.

title: Parent identity linked to child's grades
description: Parent's login credentials and account linkage to child account creates a direct link between parent identity and child's academic information, enabling tracking of parent-child relationship through the grades portal.
assumptions: Parent account is linked to child account in the system

title: Parent disclosing more than necessary
description: Parent may share child's grades without understanding the extent of information being disclosed, potentially including unnecessary metadata or related information.
assumptions: Parent may not fully understand data sharing implications

title: Flow metadata links parent to child
description: Data flow metadata (timestamps, IP addresses, request patterns) could be used to link parent identity to child's grades, even if content is encrypted.
assumptions: Network metadata is observable by third parties

title: Data in transit intercepted
description: Grades data transmitted from parent to portal could be intercepted by network attackers, potentially exposing sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Network transmission is not fully secured

title: System links parent to child through grades
description: Grades portal may create persistent linkage between parent and child accounts, enabling long-term tracking of parent-child relationship through academic data.
assumptions: System maintains parent-child linkage records

title: System discloses more than necessary
description: Portal may disclose additional information beyond requested grades, such as related student information or system metadata.
assumptions: System may have broader data access than needed

title: Lawful basis for sharing grades with parents
description: The portal may share grades without a clear legal basis or parental consent, potentially violating data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes grades are personal data requiring lawful processing basis.

title: Inaccurate or outdated grade information shared
description: The portal may display outdated, incorrect, or incomplete grade information to parents, affecting their understanding of their child's academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes grades are time-sensitive and accuracy is important.

title: Insufficient notification about data sharing
description: Parents may not be adequately informed about what data is being shared, with whom, and for what purposes.
assumptions: Assumes notification requirements exist for data sharing with parents.

title: Unintended interception of grade data in transit
description: Grade data transmitted from portal to parent could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over potentially insecure channels.

title: Parent storing more data than necessary
description: Parents may retain and store more grade-related information than necessary for their intended purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes parents may have the capability to store data beyond immediate use.

title: Unintended access to grade data by parent
description: Parents may inadvertently share grade information with unauthorized third parties or use it for purposes beyond the intended educational context.
assumptions: Assumes parents may not always use data appropriately.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing by Administrator
description: School Administrator (EE4) may share sensitive student/parent information (names, emails, roles, relationships) without proper authorization or in an insecure manner, potentially exposing confidential data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Administrator has access to sensitive account and relationship data

title: Accidental Data Disclosure by Administrator
description: School Administrator (EE4) may inadvertently disclose sensitive information while creating, modifying, or disabling accounts and parent-child links, such as accidentally including sensitive data in communications or sharing with unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Administrator may make human error or lack awareness of privacy implications

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Sensitive data (names, emails, roles, relationships) transmitted from School Administrator (EE4) to Grades Portal Web App (P1) may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing confidential information.
assumptions: Data flows over network without adequate encryption or security controls

title: Unintended Data Exposure During Transmission
description: Data in transit between School Administrator (EE4) and Grades Portal Web App (P1) may be exposed to unauthorized parties through network sniffing, man-in-the-middle attacks, or other interception methods.
assumptions: Data transmission lacks adequate security measures

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Data
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) may allow unauthorized users to access sensitive student/parent information (names, emails, roles, relationships) that has been received and stored, potentially violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: System may have inadequate access controls or authentication mechanisms

title: System-Induced Data Leakage
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) may inadvertently leak sensitive data to unauthorized parties through misconfigured interfaces, API endpoints, or other system vulnerabilities.
assumptions: System may have configuration or implementation errors

title: Inadequate Data Validation at Destination
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) may not properly validate incoming data from School Administrator (EE4), potentially storing incorrect, incomplete, or malformed data that could lead to privacy or operational issues.
assumptions: System lacks robust input validation mechanisms

title: Incorrect data written to account directory
description: The grading service may write incorrect, incomplete, or improperly validated account records and parent-child relationship links to the account directory, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Assumes the grading service has some control over data validation before writing to the directory.

title: Parent-child relationships enable user linkage
description: The parent-child relationship links written to the account directory could be used to link or identify users across different account records, potentially enabling unwanted tracking or profiling.
assumptions: Assumes the parent-child relationships are stored in a way that allows correlation between different account records.

title: Account records stored without adequate confidentiality
description: The account directory may store account records and parent-child relationship links without sufficient confidentiality controls, potentially exposing sensitive user information to unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory has some storage mechanism that could be accessed by unauthorized parties.

title: Data integrity compromised during storage
description: The account directory may not properly validate or protect the integrity of account records and parent-child relationship links during storage, allowing for potential data corruption or tampering.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory has some storage mechanism that could be compromised.

title: Data Disclosure in Transit - Third-Party Access
description: Full grade records, assignments, and account directory are transferred to a third-party cloud hosting provider. Data in transit may be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission.

title: Data Storage at Third-Party Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider receives and stores full grade records, assignments, and account directory. This creates a data disclosure risk as the third party may have access to personal data beyond the intended scope.

title: Over-Sharing of Personal Data
description: The Assignment & Grading Service transfers full grade records, assignments, and account directory to the cloud provider. This may include more personal data than strictly required for the backup and hosting replication purpose.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Data in transit between the Assignment & Grading Service and Cloud Hosting Provider may be intercepted by unauthorized parties, potentially exposing sensitive student information.

title: Grade records may be linked to student identities
description: Grade records in the database may contain or be linked to student identifiers, enabling linkage to student profiles, parents, or teachers.
assumptions: Grade records may contain student IDs or other identifiers that can be linked to individuals.

title: Sensitive information may be deduced from grade records
description: Analysis of grade records could allow deduction of sensitive information about students, such as learning disabilities or special needs.
assumptions: Grade patterns may reveal underlying conditions or special circumstances.

title: Flow metadata may enable party linking
description: Data flow metadata (e.g., timestamps, packet sizes, flow patterns) could be used to link or identify the parties involved in the data exchange.
assumptions: Network metadata may be observable and analyzable.

title: Grading service may link data to student profiles
description: The grading service may use grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views, potentially enabling linkage of data to individual profiles.
assumptions: The service processes data to create views that may be linked to individuals.

title: Unintended data processing for multiple views
description: Processing grade records to build multiple views (student, parent, teacher) may involve unintended or excessive data processing beyond the original purpose.
assumptions: Creating multiple views may involve processing beyond the original data collection purpose.
